# TREND1NG 13th-Minute Brief

The top 13 trending news stories in the universe, ranked every hour at the 13th minute UTC.
The flagship for news around the universe. Adults 21+. For entertainment purposes only.
RSS: https://channel13autoposter.github.io/trend1ng-brief-archive/feed.xml

## 2026-11-06 04:13 UTC
1. Council on Foreign Relations | COP31 opens in Antalya, Türkiye on November 9 under a joint Türkiye-Australia presidency with the United States sending no official delegation after withdrawing from the Paris Agreement, the Council on Foreign Relations reported November 5 — national climate plans point to emissions only about 6 percent below 2019 levels by 2035 against the roughly 60 percent cut a 1.5°C pathway needs, and the presidency concedes the world is likely to exceed 1.5°C within a few years.
2. World Online | Iran has sent the United States a nuclear proposal via Qatar, to be discussed only after Washington meets Tehran's conditions, World Online reported November 6 — a new mediated channel on the nuclear file while the US-Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz crisis continue.
3. The DONUT | Type 2 diabetes remission was achieved by 54 percent of people under 45 after six months of an intensive low-calorie diet and exercise programme, compared with 4 percent receiving standard care, a new study reported by The DONUT on November 5 found — a large effect from a non-drug intervention in younger patients.
4. Newsweek | South Korea has completed its first container-ship round trip between Asia and Europe via Russia's Northern Sea Route, Newsweek International reported — the PanStar Acro sailed from Busan to Britain in 20 days as disruption in the Strait of Hormuz and pressure on the Red Sea corridor push global trade toward an Arctic alternative.
5. Reuters | US stocks plunged on Thursday in an AI-trade meltdown, Reuters reported November 5 — the Nasdaq fell 5.5 percent and wiped off about 2 trillion dollars of market value, the Philadelphia chip index fell 12 percent in its second-biggest drop on record, Nvidia fell 9 percent, and Bitcoin fell 6 percent to 75,000 dollars, as investors feared a Democratic-controlled Congress will slow the data centre buildout.
6. Seoul Economic Daily | Yonsei University has brought online a quantum computer built around IBM's newest Nighthawk processor, the first Nighthawk installed at an outside institution's own facility, the Seoul Economic Daily reported November 4 citing Yonhap — 120 programmable qubits running more than 100,000 circuits per second, aimed at cutting drug-target identification from up to two years to five months.
7. Reuters | The Bank of England raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, to 4 percent, and the hawkish vote suggests more rises are likely, Reuters reported November 5 — UK borrowing costs moving up on inflation pressures from the US-Iran war while traders pushed back the expected timing of the Federal Reserve's next hike to March.
8. The DONUT | CVS will split its 117 billion dollar business into two public companies by mid-2028, separating about 9,000 retail pharmacies from its insurance business and pharmacy benefit manager, The DONUT reported November 5 — one of the largest corporate splits in history, with shares closing about 12 percent lower.
9. NASA | NASA's Hubble Space Telescope study of 37 nearby dwarf galaxies found they retain only a small fraction of the oxygen their stars made — between 4 and 25 percent, about 11 percent on average — NASA and the Space Telescope Science Institute reported November 2, with galactic winds from massive stars and supernovae apparently stripping oxygen far more effectively than current models predict.
10. NPR | NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory re-entered Earth's atmosphere over Indonesia after 22 years in space, NPR reported November 4 — a fiery end for the satellite that spent two decades racing to catch gamma-ray bursts, among the most powerful explosions in the universe, after solar activity swelled the atmosphere and dragged it out of orbit.
11. The DONUT | Scientists found what a PNAS study calls the strongest evidence yet of preserved dinosaur red blood cells, in a fossil of Aratasaurus museunacionali, a theropod that lived in present-day Brazil about 115 million years ago, The DONUT reported November 5 — microscopic structures resembling red blood cells inside the ancient bone.
12. Reuters | Pope Leo departs Rome on November 6 for a visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru running to November 17, Reuters reported in its November 5 diary of political and general news events — an eleven-day Latin America tour by the pontiff.
13. CareerIndia | Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football at age 41, CareerIndia reported November 6 — he finishes with 234 appearances and 146 goals for Portugal, the highest-scoring player in men's international football history.

## 2026-11-05 20:13 UTC
1. SiliconANGLE | IBM, AMD and the Quantum Science Center at Oak Ridge National Laboratory launched a co-design platform for quantum error correction pairing IBM's 120-qubit Nighthawk processor with Oak Ridge's Umbra supercomputer, SiliconANGLE reported November 5 — tied to the Department of Energy Quantum Genesis goal of 100 logical qubits running 100,000 hard operations by late 2028, against 70 logical qubits and 438 hard operations demonstrated so far.
2. Fivly | A cyberattack on a refrigeration supplier for France's national blood service was thwarted after it targeted cold-room systems on Monday and pushed temperatures to extreme levels, Fivly reported November 5 — an attack on the cold chain behind a national blood supply.
3. Reuters | Democrats will hold at least 54 Senate seats and gained at least 30 House seats in the midterms, with Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi still uncalled, Reuters reported via Level Headlines on November 5 — an updated count cementing Democratic control of both chambers, while President Trump said he would likely get along with them but holds the veto.
4. Associated Press | A tanker was hit by two projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, late Wednesday, the UK Maritime Trade Operations Center said via Associated Press reporting on November 5 — crew status and damage unconfirmed, a new strike near the Strait of Hormuz energy chokepoint.
5. Montgomery Advertiser | NASA's Artemis II crewed Moon launch and two later engine burns created three ionosphere disturbances stretching about 3,100 miles and 50 degrees of longitude across North America, researchers at National Cheng Kung University in Taiwan found, the Montgomery Advertiser reported November 5 — changes large enough for GPS errors of several metres, with no widespread outage found.
6. Kyiv Post | Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles overnight November 2-3, mainly at power plants and substations in nine Ukrainian regions, President Zelenskyy said via Kyiv Post reporting — described as the largest attack on Ukraine's power grid this year.
7. SPA | Saudi Arabia's defence ministry signed a cooperation agreement with its Syrian counterpart, Saudi state news agency SPA reported via Just Security on November 5 — a formal defence link between Riyadh and Damascus reshaping regional alignments.
8. Associated Press | Bangladesh's ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina told AP News she remains committed to returning to Bangladesh next month despite being sentenced to death over her government's deadly crackdown on protesters, Just Security reported November 5 citing AP.
9. Just Security | China is sending its Middle East envoy Zhai Jun to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia in early and mid-November, China's foreign ministry said, reported November 5 — Beijing working the Gulf capitals as the US-Iran war and Hormuz crisis continue.
10. Associated Press | Russia and Ukraine exchanged airstrikes overnight as talks resumed in Brussels on Thursday on Ukraine's postwar rebuilding and security guarantees, the Associated Press reported November 5 — with separate US-hosted trilateral talks planned in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11.
11. Fivly | Eurozone inflation rose to 4 percent in October, a three-year high, Fivly reported November 5 — surging energy costs drove the increase while core inflation remained steady.
12. Just Security | Polish authorities arrested four people on charges of spying for Russian intelligence services and providing them with military components, Poland's Internal Security Agency said via Just Security on November 5 — two others accused of participating in an organised criminal group were placed under non-custodial preventive measures.
13. Just Security | The US Treasury Department issued new sanctions against companies and individuals based in India and Turkey for their support of Iran, Just Security reported November 5 — widening the sanctions net beyond Iran itself to its overseas support networks.

## 2026-11-05 12:13 UTC
1. WHO | The World Health Organization endorsed trials of two new vaccines amid the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, WHO action reported November 5 — a vaccine path opened while a British healthcare worker from the outbreak zone was already being evacuated to the UK.
2. Seven Lights | Voters rebuked AI data centres 44 to 1 at the US midterm ballot, Seven Lights reported November 5, with one exception in North Dakota — a lopsided local backlash against the infrastructure behind the AI buildout, on the same ballot that reshaped Congress.
3. EIN Presswire | Alice & Bob set a record low for the quantum resources needed to break internet encryption, EIN Presswire reported November 2 via AiThority — 23,000 physical qubits running for three days could break RSA-2048, and 30,000 could crack a Bitcoin key, sharply lowering the projected hardware bar.
4. Carbon Brief | Brazil's roadmap to end tropical deforestation by 2030, backed by 93 countries, prices the job at 300 billion dollars a year by 2030, Carbon Brief reported — while its Tropical Forest Forever Facility remains billions short of its 125 billion dollar target.
5. XTB | Vice President JD Vance blamed the war with Iran for the Republican midterm defeat, writing that 'the reason we lost is the war,' XTB reported November 5 — the plainest public break yet with President Trump's foreign policy, as Trump said he would do it again.
6. XTB | The Dow surged more than 1,570 points, about 3 percent, in its best day since April 2025, while Brent crude fell almost 9 percent to settle at 94.62 dollars a barrel and WTI dropped more than 8 percent to 88.12 dollars, XTB reported November 5 — markets rallying as traders bet the clear midterm result would speed efforts to end the Iran war.
7. Financial Times | Chinese authorities have refused to approve SoftBank's 5.4 billion dollar acquisition of ABB's robotics division, the Financial Times reported via XTB on November 5 — a blocked deal at the centre of the global robotics race.
8. BURN VOC | SpaceX signed a multiyear deal for Qualcomm Dragonwing gear at tens of thousands of US cell sites for Starlink Mobile, BURN VOC reported November 5, with rollout starting in 2027 — satellite connectivity moving directly into the US mobile network buildout.
9. Wall Street Journal | El Salvador has airlifted more than 2,500 troops and special forces to Haiti, now patrolling Port-au-Prince as the largest armed contingent in the country, the Wall Street Journal reported via a November 5 news roundup — President Bukele's high-stakes deployment after an ambush left four Salvadoran technicians missing.
10. Reuters | Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 years in prison after pleading guilty to conspiring to collude with foreign forces under the national security law, Reuters reported November 5 — his second national security case and one of the heaviest sentences yet under the law.
11. Phys.org | The James Webb Space Telescope's young massive clusters in the Cosmic Gems arc and Firefly Sparkle galaxy may be the birthplaces of intermediate-mass black holes, Phys.org reported November 3 from Astronomy and Astrophysics research — clusters yielding black holes of 1,600 to 2,700 solar masses, a possible origin for heavy black hole seeds in the early universe.
12. The Hindu | Russian drone and missile attacks disrupted electricity and water services in Kyiv and the death toll in Komyshuvakha rose to 40, The Hindu reported November 5 — a rising toll from the aid-centre strike first briefed at 37 dead, with President Zelenskyy saying the attack may have killed around 70 people and renewing his plea for air defences.
13. Bloomberg | Binance said the hackers behind the historic 6.3 billion dollar heist of its crypto holdings used social engineering techniques including fake job interviews, Bloomberg reported in the exchange's most detailed account yet of how the incident unfolded, reported November 5.

## 2026-11-05 04:13 UTC
1. RFE/RL | The United States struck Iran's strategic Qeshm Island in a series of previously undisclosed attacks carried out on the eve of the US midterm elections, RFE/RL reported — the strikes emerged even as President Trump played down the prospect of renewed war and signalled hope for a diplomatic deal with Tehran.
2. France 24 | Iran said four oil tankers were destroyed after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and that two other vessels were seized, France 24 reported via Hansen Intel — an Iranian claim, made a day after President Trump said the United States had launched strikes on Iran, over the chokepoint that carries a large share of world oil trade.
3. RFE/RL | First Lady Melania Trump will host Russian and Ukrainian representatives at the White House on November 5 following a localised cease-fire in Ukraine's Kherson region, and the United States will host a new round of Russia-Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11, RFE/RL reported — analysts cautioned that deep divisions over a cease-fire and security guarantees make a major breakthrough unlikely.
4. Quantum Computing Report | Automated AI agents deployed by researchers from IBM Quantum, QuICS and MIT uncovered 699 magic-state factory classes, including 564 previously unknown protocols, Quantum Computing Report reported — sharply reducing the hardware overhead projected for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
5. Quantum Zeitgeist | NVIDIA researchers demonstrated an AI-assisted workflow, verified with the Lean formal-verification tool, that mapped an eight-qubit toric code onto a model of a superconducting device and connected a quantum code space to the device's low-energy states for the first time, Quantum Zeitgeist reported — a reusable route to designing quantum error-correction codes directly onto hardware.
6. ScienceDaily | NASA's Voyager 1 has reached one light-day from Earth, about 16.09 billion miles, ScienceDaily reported — the most distant human-made object now sits a full day's light-travel away, making its radio round trip about 48 hours.
7. Reuters | The death toll from a Russian bombing of an aid distribution point in Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhzhia region rose to 37 with dozens still missing, Reuters reported — one of the deadliest strikes on civilians this year, as Kyiv said the aid hub was hit multiple times.
8. AFP | US House Speaker Mike Johnson will step down as Republican leader following his party's heavy midterm defeat, his spokesperson confirmed to AFP, as Reuters separately reported Republican allies and strategists urging President Trump to overhaul White House personnel and abandon policies they blame for the losses, including on Iran and tariffs — Trump ruled out removing Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.
9. Stockbiz | North Korea tested a newly designed anti-aircraft missile system and held a strategic cruise missile strike drill, North Korean state media reported on November 5 via Stockbiz — the latest weapons display as US-mediated diplomacy moves on multiple fronts.
10. Stockbiz | French regional bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa was hit by a cyberattack that led to fraudulent transactions totalling around 100 million euros, Stockbiz reported November 5 — a nine-figure theft from a single regional lender.
11. The Guardian | A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK, The Guardian reported via Hansen Intel — an international medical evacuation out of the outbreak zone.
12. Dhyeya IAS | Astronomers using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope and Chandra X-ray Observatory found LID-568, a black hole about 1.5 billion years after the Big Bang feeding at nearly 40 times the Eddington limit long treated as a ceiling, Dhyeya IAS reported — super-Eddington growth on a scale previously thought impossible, challenging theories of how early black holes formed.
13. Reuters | British sport is dangerously under-prepared for climate change, a British Association for Sustainable Sport report found, Reuters reported November 5 — every organisation surveyed was affected by extreme weather in 2026, 27 percent of professional stadiums analysed in England face high direct flood risk rising to a projected 35 percent, and nearly three-quarters of people hit by this year's heatwaves did less sport and physical activity.

## 2026-11-04 20:13 UTC
1. Phys.org | Six proven climate and health measures could save nearly 1.6 million lives a year and generate trillions in economic and fiscal benefits, the World Health Organization reported November 4 ahead of COP31 — heat early warnings, climate-resilient water and sanitation, hygiene, cleaner household fuels and fossil-fuel pricing, with pricing alone estimated to prevent 1.2 million deaths a year.
2. Reuters | Rich countries are falling far short on climate adaptation funding, a UN report found November 4 — developed-country funding rose only to 28.2 billion dollars in 2024 against about 305 billion dollars needed each year by developing nations, ahead of COP31 opening in Antalya on November 9 as warming heads past 1.5C.
3. Menlo Ventures | Enterprise AI deployment spending reached 176.8 billion dollars by September 2026, up from 33 billion dollars last year, Menlo Ventures reported in its fourth annual State of Enterprise AI report on November 3 — a more than fivefold jump in one year, with AI agents burning most of the tokens.
4. Just Security | President Trump told the New York Times he was absolutely willing to accept the midterm election results and prepared to work with Democrats, and separately acknowledged the Iran war played a role in his party's defeat, Just Security reported November 4 — a new development after Democrats took control of Congress.
5. GazeWire | China's Jiuzhang 4.0 photonic quantum computer won a World Internet Conference science award in Wuzhen, GazeWire reported November 4 citing CGTN — the University of Science and Technology of China machine fed 1,024 beams of squeezed light into an 8,176-channel circuit and recorded up to 3,050 photons in a single run, up from 255 for Jiuzhang 3.0.
6. Applied Physics Reviews | One extra measurement before a run of operations cut a superconducting qubit's average error rate from about 0.14 percent to 0.065 percent, researchers reported in Applied Physics Reviews — a reduction of about 54 percent, and up to 77 percent against the largest error observed without the real-time feedback check.
7. Scientific American | New FLIP software that models the James Webb Space Telescope's tiny wobble made the observatory two to 15 times more sensitive to faint exoplanets and revealed the giant planet 51 Eridani b hidden in existing data, Scientific American reported November 4 from a Nature study — a path toward imaging worlds closer to their stars.
8. Just Security | Poland has launched a special operation involving counterterrorism police, intelligence officers and increased border security on its northern frontier with Russia, Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced, Just Security reported November 4.
9. HPCwire | D-Wave's enhanced Stride hybrid solver found better solutions in 15 seconds than its previous version found in 120 seconds, HPCwire reported November 4 — on travelling-salesperson problems up to 10,000 locations its solutions averaged within 0.02 percent of the best possible result and more than 200 times closer than the prior solver at the same runtime.
10. Just Security | Spain's Transport Minister Oscar Puente resigned six days after a high-speed train collision killed at least 69 people and injured dozens more, Just Security reported November 4.
11. Scientific American | NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory ended more than two decades studying gamma-ray bursts by re-entering Earth's atmosphere in the early hours of November 4, Scientific American reported — most of the 3,200-pound telescope was expected to burn up after a rescue mission to boost its orbit failed in July.
12. Science | Teghaza 001, a rose-coloured meteorite found in the Sahara in 2022, is a piece of Mars altered by water more than 4.1 billion years ago and one of the oldest Martian meteorites ever found, researchers reported in Science — NASA-funded dating of its minerals gives a rare snapshot of Mars' ancient crust.
13. UT San Antonio Today | Minerals exposed to simulated Venus surface conditions for 60 days in NASA's Glenn Extreme Environment Rig formed fluorine-bearing micas and magnesite that could preserve evidence Venus was once much wetter, UT San Antonio reported November 4 — giving the coming DAVINCI, VERITAS and EnVision missions specific mineral targets to look for.

CNN | President Trump has reached a deal with Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu to wind down 4 billion dollars in annual US military aid to Israel by the end of the year, CNN reported via International Intrigue — ending an Obama-era agreement not due to expire until 2028, with Israeli officials yet to comment.
3. Seoul Economic Daily | Yonsei University brought online a quantum computer built on IBM's newest Nighthawk processor, the first installed at an outside institution, Seoul Economic Daily reported November 4 citing Yonhap — 120 programmable qubits and 25 times the circuit throughput of the prior generation, aimed at cutting drug-target identification from up to two years to five months.
4. Financial Times | Nvidia has told its data centre partners to reduce their China exposure and ensure at least 51 percent of revenue comes from clients outside China, the Financial Times reported via International Intrigue — a verbal cap reshaping where the AI chip supply chain can sell.

6. GlobeNewswire | Quantum X Labs demonstrated its Qatacomb quantum encryption scheme on a real 156-qubit IBM Quantum Heron r2 processor, GlobeNewswire reported November 3 — the intended recipient recovered the encrypted image while an adversary without the key gained no usable information, a privacy guarantee designed to hold regardless of adversary computing power.
7. Reuters | Authorities diverted, inspected and scrambled fighter jets to escort at least seven flights across Italy, Poland, Bulgaria and Spain plus an Israel-bound cruise ship in Greece after a coordinated wave of bomb threats later confirmed as hoaxes, Reuters reported via International Intrigue.

Malay Mail | Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto sacked his chief of staff and former police chief a day after his arrest alongside two senior officers for allegedly wiretapping the president, senior officials and journalists, Malay Mail reported via International Intrigue — advisors warned the alleged conduct could amount to treason.
9. UN News | Senior UN officials warned of catastrophic consequences as drone attacks on civilian infrastructure intensify across Sudan, UN News reported November 4 — attacks deepening an already severe humanitarian crisis.
10. NASA | Thirty-seven nearby dwarf galaxies retain only 4 to 25 percent, on average about 11 percent, of the oxygen their stars produced, a Hubble Space Telescope study published November 2 found, NASA data showed — supernova winds appear to eject oxygen far more efficiently than current galaxy-evolution models predict.
11. The Guardian | European Commission President von der Leyen and Canada's Prime Minister Carney used their Montreal summit to launch a new Alliance for the Future, billed as a protective canopy against geopolitical turmoil, The Guardian reported via International Intrigue.
12. Korea JoongAng Daily | A South Korean foreign ministry employee accidentally uploaded passport details for President Lee and dozens of senior officials to a malware-scanning platform, granting access to security researchers worldwide and potentially adversaries, Korea JoongAng Daily reported via International Intrigue.
13. Medical Xpress | Quantum machine learning models predicted lung cancer from limited symptom and risk-factor data with up to 94.31 percent accuracy in simulation and 91.90 percent on D-Wave quantum hardware, Medical Xpress reported November 2 citing Discover Quantum Science — preliminary results, not based on medical images or pathology, for settings where training data is scarce.

## 2026-11-04 04:13 UTC
1. Reuters | The world faces a financing gap of about 30 trillion euros over the next five years, Santander reported November 3 — total investment needs for 2026 to 2030 are estimated at about 50 trillion euros, with climate mitigation and adaptation alone accounting for 22 to 26 trillion euros of the gap, alongside AI, defence, ageing and healthcare pressures, ahead of the UN climate summit opening in Antalya on November 9.
2. USA Today | Democrats flipped US Senate seats in Texas, South Carolina and North Carolina on November 3, USA Today reported — James Talarico defeated Ken Paxton in Texas, Annie Andrews defeated Darline Graham in South Carolina and Roy Cooper won in North Carolina, leaving Democrats needing one more flip to erase the Republicans' 53-47 Senate majority.
3. AlphaSignal | Researchers at the Institute of Science Tokyo reported their Auctopus system of LLM agents ran a quantum physics study end to end, AlphaSignal reported November 2 — the agents generated 75 proposals, rejected 74, derived an exact calibration law for NV-centre ensembles in diamond, checked it on a supercomputer and tested its prediction on physical quantum hardware.
4. OneWorld SouthAsia | Afghanistan's opium cultivation surged 325 percent in 2026 despite the Taliban ban, OneWorld SouthAsia reported November 4 citing UN reporting — a sharp reversal under prohibition in the country that has historically supplied most of the world's opium.
5. CNN | Democrats were projected to retake control of the US House of Representatives in the November 3 midterms, CNN reported — a result that would create divided government for the final two years of President Trump's term, with CNN noting Trump's 2024 margins fell sharply in rural districts and heavily Latino districts flipped or held for Democrats.
6. Reuters | China secured 45 billion dollars in clean industry investment in 2026 and now accounts for 49 percent of all clean industrial plants operating or under construction worldwide, Reuters reported November 4 citing the Mission Possible Partnership tracker — a record 36 commercial-scale decarbonisation projects reached final investment decision in the past 12 months, 23 of them in China.
7. OneWorld SouthAsia | Climate change is redrawing India's disease map as mosquitoes climb the Himalayas, OneWorld SouthAsia reported November 3 — vector-borne disease risk moving into higher, previously cooler regions as temperatures rise.
8. OneWorld SouthAsia | Farmers in Vietnam's Mekong Delta are turning to saltwater as rising seas and upstream dams reshape the country's rice bowl, OneWorld SouthAsia reported — salinity changing what the delta that feeds much of Vietnam can grow.
9. NASA | NASA's twin ESCAPADE spacecraft will attempt the first powered flyby of Earth by Mars-bound spacecraft, NASA reported November 2 — each craft combines Earth's gravity with an engine burn on November 7 and November 9 to gain more than 1,000 miles per hour, then cruises ten months to Mars to study how the solar wind drives atmospheric loss.
10. Reuters | Markets reacted swiftly to the US midterm results, Reuters reported November 4 — US stock futures declined sharply, Treasury yields dipped and the dollar moved lower as analysts priced in a stronger-than-expected Democratic showing and the prospect of divided government.
11. CNN | Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won Georgia's governorship, becoming the first Black woman elected governor in American history, CNN reported November 3 — she defeated the Trump-endorsed Republican candidate as Democrats also held the state's US Senate seat.
12. Reuters | New Zealand's ruling National Party and opposition Labour are in a dead heat days before the November 7 general election, Reuters reported November 3 — the final 1News Verian poll put National at 30 percent and Labour at 29 percent, with no clear winner in the tightly contested vote.
13. USA Today | Democrat Amy Acton defeated Republican Vivek Ramaswamy to win Ohio's governorship, USA Today reported November 3 — Acton led Ohio's health department during the early COVID-19 pandemic, and the result was another statewide Democratic win on a night of broad gains.

Shared Sapience | GPT-6 Astra edited 0.016 percent of a small open model's weights to lift MATH-500 accuracy from 7.9 percent to 48.1 percent and instruction-following from 21.0 percent to 62.3 percent without gradient training or sight of the test problems, Shared Sapience reported November 3 — a model directly repairing another model's reasoning by editing its weights.

Reuters | Brazil is ending its year-long COP30 presidency with roadmaps aimed at curbing deforestation and accelerating a shift away from fossil fuels ahead of COP31 opening in Antalya on November 9, Reuters reported November 3 — COP30 President Andre Correa do Lago said governments must integrate climate goals into policymaking as a UN report showed 1.5C increasingly out of reach.

Reuters | Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have advanced to within 50 miles of Aden, the temporary capital and stronghold of Yemen's internationally recognised government, military sources told Reuters, reported November 3 via Just Security — a major shift in Yemen's war toward the government's seat.
10. Phys.org | Converting nonforested land into planted forests was associated with an average 26 percent increase in fire occurrence per hectare per year and a 23 percent increase in expected burned area, a PNAS study of 67,248 planted-forest patches from 2001 to 2023 found, Phys.org reported November 3 — tree planting's carbon benefits can be undermined by wildfire depending on location.
11. HPCwire | Quint Computing raised 9.1 million euros plus a 2.2 million euro European Innovation Council Pathfinder grant for a superconducting chip architecture that prevents most errors at the hardware level, HPCwire reported November 3 — the German startup says the approach could cut fault-tolerant quantum complexity, overhead and energy use by a factor of 100.
12. Daily Brief | Russia launched 289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles at nine Ukrainian regions overnight, killing at least one person and triggering emergency power cuts, while a Russian aerial bomb hit a hospital in Kharkiv injuring 73 and the Komyshuvakha aid-site toll rose to at least 29 killed and 48 missing, Daily Brief reported November 3.
13. Phys.org | Young massive clusters in the Firefly Sparkle galaxy seen by the James Webb Space Telescope about 600 million years after the Big Bang could be factories for the heavy seeds that grow into supermassive black holes, research in Astronomy and Astrophysics found, Phys.org reported November 3 — a possible origin for the early universe's oversized black holes.

## 2026-11-03 12:13 UTC
1. Phys.org | Two UN reports warned exceeding 1.5C of warming will bring large-scale and in many cases irreversible impacts for Earth's cryosphere — glaciers, sea ice and permafrost — Phys.org reported November 2 — with warming already at 1.37C, sea-level rise potentially reaching 5 centimetres a year by 2150 in an overshoot path and permafrost thaw releasing carbon on a national scale.
2. Le Monde | A 'super El Niño' that began in the equatorial Pacific in spring has already reached unprecedented levels since the late 20th century, Le Monde reported November 3 — Bolivia declared a state of emergency October 31 amid severe drought, with massive wildfires in Indonesia, historic drought in French Guiana and hurricanes in Mexico ahead of an expected peak at year's end.
3. Reuters | The United States will bring Russian and Ukrainian representatives together in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 for another round of peace negotiations, Reuters reported via Open Chronicle November 3 — US envoy Steve Witkoff said talks would address security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian measures, with the Kremlin confirming Vladimir Medinsky will lead Moscow's delegation.
4. Seven Lights Daily Brief | Dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries reported suspected cyber-attacks on refrigeration systems overnight, Seven Lights Daily Brief reported November 3 — about 40 Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg plus shops in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland had freezers switched to defrost, spoiling stock, in a method matching an October attack on hundreds of French supermarkets.
5. Seven Lights Daily Brief | The US Supreme Court refused in a one-sentence unsigned order to set aside 20,000 California mail ballots the Trump administration alleged were cast by likely non-citizens, Seven Lights Daily Brief reported November 3 — the administration had lost at every lower level, with a district judge finding its identification process rife with errors and the Ninth Circuit holding election authority rests with states and Congress.
6. Open Chronicle | Australia's High Court began examining constitutional challenges to the country's under-16 social media ban, Open Chronicle reported November 3 — Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project argue the December 2025 law burdens political communication, the government cites child protection, and nearly five million accounts have been blocked since the law took effect.
7. Quantum Zeitgeist | A new feature map by Vincent Gurgul of Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin and David Prinz of Universität Bonn boosts quantum neural network accuracy by up to 44 percent on benchmark datasets, Quantum Zeitgeist reported — the method removes amplitude encoding's scale-invariance limit while keeping logarithmic qubit scaling, narrowing the gap with classical neural networks.
8.
